attrs.label: What does a performance marketing agency actually do?
attrs.html:
What does a performance marketing agency actually do?

A performance marketing agency plans, runs and improves paid ads where you pay for measurable results, such as leads and sales, rather than for being seen. It sets up tracking, chooses the platforms, writes and tests the ads, and moves budget to whatever brings customers at the lowest cost.

  • Paid search, social, video and marketplace ads
  • Conversion tracking connected to your CRM
  • Landing pages and creative that turn clicks into enquiries
  • Reports in cost per lead, sales and return on ad spend
Performance marketing compared with brand advertising
QuestionPerformance marketingBrand advertising
What you pay forResults: leads, sales, bookingsReach: views and impressions
How success is measuredCost per lead or sale, return on ad spendAwareness and brand recall
How fast you see itWithin weeksOver months or years
Main channelsGoogle, Meta, LinkedIn, TikTok, AmazonTV, outdoor, sponsorship

attrs.label: Why paid ads stop paying
attrs.html:
Why paid ads stop paying

The same seven problems turn up in almost every account we audit. Pick one to see how we fix it.

The challengeBudget leaks into irrelevant searches, broad audiences and placements that never convert.

Our approach

Find the waste first, then move that money to what already works.

Most accounts we audit waste between a fifth and a third of their budget. The fix is rarely clever: it’s regular, careful housekeeping.

In practice

  • Search terms reviewed every week and poor ones excluded
  • Display and app placements checked and blocked
  • Broad audiences narrowed using your customer data
  • Budget moved monthly to the lowest cost per sale

Why it matters

Cutting waste is the fastest win in any account. The money is already in your budget.

Methods we use

  1. 1Search term review

    Every search you paid for, with the ones that never convert excluded.

  2. 2Placement clean-up

    Apps, sites and audiences that eat budget, removed.

  3. 3Budget by result

    Money moved to the campaigns with the lowest cost per sale.

  4. 4Weekly checks

    Spend watched every week, not once a month.

What you get

  • A waste report
  • A negative keyword list
  • A budget plan

The challengePlatforms over-count, double-count or miss conversions, so nobody knows what’s working.

Our approach

Make every conversion count once, and match it to your CRM.

If tracking is wrong, every decision after it is wrong too. Platforms optimise towards whatever you tell them is a conversion.

In practice

  • Each conversion action checked to fire once, at the right moment
  • Enhanced conversions and the Conversions API set up
  • Offline conversions sent back from your CRM
  • A test report you can keep

Why it matters

Good tracking is what lets Google and Meta find more of your best customers.

Methods we use

  1. 1Tracking audit

    Every tag, event and conversion action checked.

  2. 2Server-side tracking

    Conversions API and server-side tags that survive ad blockers.

  3. 3CRM connection

    Offline conversions sent back, so platforms learn which leads became sales.

  4. 4A test report

    Proof that each conversion fires once, with screenshots.

What you get

  • A tracking audit
  • Tested conversion setup
  • CRM-matched reporting

The challengeCampaigns optimise for cheap form fills, and sales spends its week chasing people who were never going to buy.

Our approach

Optimise for customers, not form fills.

Cheap leads are easy. Leads that become customers take more work: better forms, better signals and better feedback.

In practice

  • Forms that ask one or two qualifying questions
  • Lead values sent to the platforms
  • Sales outcomes fed back weekly
  • Landing pages that set clear expectations

Why it matters

A lead that costs twice as much but buys three times as often is a better deal.

Methods we use

  1. 1Qualifying questions

    Forms that filter out poor leads before they reach sales.

  2. 2Value-based bidding

    Platforms told what each lead was worth.

  3. 3Lead scoring feedback

    Sales outcomes sent back to Google and Meta.

  4. 4Landing page tests

    Pages that set the right expectations.

What you get

  • Better lead quality
  • Value-based bidding
  • Lead feedback loop

The challengeGoogle Ads with one freelancer, Meta with another, LinkedIn in-house. Nobody sees the whole picture.

Our approach

One plan across every platform, with one report.

Buyers move between Google, Instagram, LinkedIn and YouTube before they enquire. Your campaigns should work together the same way.

In practice

  • A channel plan that gives each platform a clear job
  • Audiences and exclusions shared across platforms
  • Budget compared across platforms by cost per sale
  • One report and one specialist

Why it matters

When platforms are planned together, each one does its job and they stop claiming the same sale.

Methods we use

  1. 1Channel plan

    The job each platform does, from first touch to sale.

  2. 2Shared audiences

    Remarketing and exclusions coordinated across platforms.

  3. 3One budget view

    Spend and results for every platform side by side.

  4. 4One report

    One monthly report and one call.

What you get

  • A cross-platform plan
  • One dashboard
  • One point of contact

The challengeThe same three ads run for months. Costs creep up as people stop noticing them.

Our approach

Keep new creative flowing, and test it properly.

On social platforms, the ad is the targeting. Fresh creative is the biggest lever on cost per result.

In practice

  • New concepts every month, made by our designers
  • Clear tests: hook, offer, format, one at a time
  • Winners scaled, losers paused quickly
  • Learnings shared in your monthly report

Why it matters

Accounts with a steady flow of new ads keep costs down as they grow.

Methods we use

  1. 1Monthly creative

    New images, videos and copy every month.

  2. 2Structured tests

    One change at a time, so you know what worked.

  3. 3Creative reports

    Which hooks, offers and formats win.

  4. 4Design in-house

    Our designers make the ads, so there’s no waiting.

What you get

  • New ads every month
  • A testing calendar
  • Creative learnings

The challengeAds send people to a homepage or a slow page that doesn’t match the ad.

Our approach

Landing pages built for the ad, and tested.

Most landing pages lose more customers than the ads ever do. Because we build websites, we fix the page as well as the ad.

In practice

  • A page for each campaign or offer
  • Fast, mobile-first pages
  • Forms with as few fields as possible
  • Tests on headlines, offers and forms

Why it matters

Doubling the conversion rate halves the cost per lead, without spending a cent more on ads.

Methods we use

  1. 1Message match

    The page repeats what the ad promised.

  2. 2Speed

    Pages that load in under two seconds on a phone.

  3. 3One clear action

    One form, one button, no distractions.

  4. 4A/B tests

    Headlines, forms and offers tested on real traffic.

What you get

  • Ad-specific landing pages
  • Speed fixes
  • Monthly tests

The challengeMonthly reports full of impressions and click-through rates, but nothing about sales.

Our approach

Report what the business cares about.

A good report answers three questions: what did we spend, what did it bring in, and what are we doing next?

In practice

  • Goals agreed before we start
  • A dashboard you can check any day
  • A one-page monthly summary
  • A monthly call with your specialist

Why it matters

When everyone can see what the ads bring in, decisions about budget get easy.

Methods we use

  1. 1Agreed goals

    Cost per lead, cost per sale and return on ad spend, agreed up front.

  2. 2A live dashboard

    Spend and results by platform, updated daily.

  3. 3Plain-English report

    What happened, why, and what we’ll do next.

  4. 4Monthly call

    Thirty minutes with your specialist.

What you get

  • A live dashboard
  • A monthly report
  • A monthly call

attrs.label: How to choose a performance marketing agency
attrs.html:
How to choose a performance marketing agency

What to expect from a good agency, what to avoid, and the questions worth asking before you hand over your budget.

What you get with us

  • Ads run in your account. You own it, the data and the history
  • Conversion tracking is checked and tested before we scale spend
  • Monthly reports in leads, sales and cost per result, not just clicks
  • A named specialist who knows your account, not a rotating team
  • A written plan for the first 90 days before we start

What we never do

  • Lock you into long contracts or keep your account if you leave
  • Take a hidden cut of your ad spend
  • Report impressions and clicks as if they were results
  • Promise rankings, results or approval from the platform
  • Change budgets or targeting without telling you

Questions to ask any performance marketing agency

Ask every agency you speak to, including us. The answers tell you more than any proposal.

  1. Q1

    Who will manage my account day to day?

    Why ask: Many agencies sell with senior people and hand the work to juniors. You want to know who makes the changes, and how much experience they have.

  2. Q2

    Will the account be in my name, and do I keep it if we part ways?

    Why ask: Your account history is valuable. If the agency owns the account, you can lose years of data and learning when you leave.

  3. Q3

    How do you charge, and do you take a percentage of ad spend?

    Why ask: A percentage of spend rewards spending more, not spending well. Know exactly what you pay and what it covers.

  4. Q4

    How will you check our conversion tracking before spending more?

    Why ask: If tracking is wrong, every bid and every report is wrong too. A good agency checks it first.

  5. Q5

    What will you report on each month?

    Why ask: Clicks and impressions are easy to grow. Ask for leads, sales, cost per result and what changed.

  6. Q6

    What exactly happens in the first 90 days?

    Why ask: A clear plan shows they have looked at your account. A vague answer usually means a template.

  7. Q7

    Can you show results for a business like ours?

    Why ask: Results in your industry, or with a similar sales cycle and budget, tell you far more than a list of logos.

  8. Q8

    What is the notice period, and is there a minimum term?

    Why ask: Long lock-ins protect the agency, not you. Good agencies keep clients because of results.

items.question: What is a performance marketing agency?
items.answer: A performance marketing agency runs paid ads where you pay for measurable results, such as leads and sales. It sets up tracking, chooses platforms, writes and tests ads, and moves budget to what brings customers at the lowest cost.

items.question: What is the difference between performance marketing and digital marketing?
items.answer: Digital marketing covers everything online, including SEO, content and email. Performance marketing is the paid part that’s measured by results: leads, sales and return on ad spend.

items.question: How much does a performance marketing agency cost?
items.answer: Most agencies charge a monthly management fee on top of your ad spend. We quote a fixed monthly fee after a free call, based on the platforms and the work involved. We never take a hidden cut of your ad spend.

items.question: Which ad platforms should my business use?
items.answer: It depends on who buys from you. Google and Microsoft catch people searching, Meta and TikTok create demand, LinkedIn reaches business buyers, and Amazon and Shopping ads sell products. We recommend a mix after the audit.

items.question: How long before paid ads bring results?
items.answer: Search campaigns usually bring leads in the first few weeks. Most accounts take two to three months of testing to settle at a good cost per lead.

items.question: Do I keep my ad accounts if I leave?
items.answer: Yes. Ads run in accounts you own. If you ever leave, you keep the accounts, the data and the history.

items.question: What is a good return on ad spend?
items.answer: It depends on your margins. A business with 60% margins can be profitable at 2×, while one with 20% margins may need 5× or more. We agree a target based on your numbers.
